title: Choose JOBE’s visual world
question: Choose the world that should make founder-led technical judgment unmistakable while architecture diagrams and scorecards carry the proof.

options.label: Systems Wayfinding
options.lineage: infrastructure control maps and international wayfinding systems
options.thesis: João turns a complex system into one legible route from symptoms to a directed engineering decision.
options.viewport: An oversized JOBE proposition intersects a deep-blue systems map; João’s concise verdict sits on the decision path and the booking action anchors the route legend.
options.risk: Can feel like public-transport branding if route lines become decorative instead of encoding the diagnostic method.

options.label: Principal’s Desktop
options.thesis: The homepage behaves like João’s analysis desktop, with each system concern opened, inspected, and resolved in crisp evidence windows.
options.case: Strong audience identification and clear diagnostic behavior; loses some contemporary authority if the retro grammar becomes the subject.
options.viewport: A blue-and-white principal workstation layers an architecture map, scorecard, and terse founder note around the real headline and primary action.
options.risk: Retro interface nostalgia can overshadow the offer and make a senior practice feel like a developer toy.

options.label: Decision Cutting Bench
options.lineage: film editing benches and marked work prints
options.thesis: Senior judgment appears as editing: competing technical paths remain visible while João marks the one worth committing to.
options.case: Excellent expression of judgment and direction; weaker audience identification because its native world is cinema rather than engineering.
options.viewport: A horizontal evidence rail crosses a dark field, showing system frames, rejected paths, and one blue committed route beneath the JOBE proposition.
options.risk: The editing metaphor fuses poorly if visitors must decode film language before understanding the consultancy.

options.label: Founder’s Technical Folio
options.lineage: bound engineering folios and tactile reading shelves
options.thesis: Architecture reviews and scorecards become a founder-kept body of work, handled as durable objects rather than disposable slides.
options.case: Strong founder-led craftsmanship; weaker product clarity because leather and paper imply heritage more readily than modern production engineering.
options.viewport: A dark-blue technical folio opens onto an architecture plate and scorecard, with João’s judgment written as restrained marginal annotations.
options.risk: Tactile skeuomorphism can feel expensive but backward-looking, especially for AI and mobile product work.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A restrained engineering-consultancy site with a split hero, technical motif, service cards, and polished blue-on-white system.
canonCard.viewport: The current expected arrangement, rebuilt at exceptional craft but intentionally familiar.
canonCard.risk: Trustworthy and clear, but it preserves the visual sameness this redesign is meant to solve.
